_meta.indication: Treatment of Philadelphia chromosome-negative relapsed or refractory B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL); approved under accelerated approval

pivotal_trials.population: Adults (age ≥18 years) with Philadelphia chromosome-negative relapsed or refractory B-cell precursor ALL with ≥10% marrow blasts
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Complete remission/complete remission with partial hematological recovery (CR/CRh*) rate within 2 cycles, with prespecified efficacy threshold of 30%
pivotal_trials.n: 185 eligible patients treated in the core study
pivotal_trials.result: CR/CRh* rate 41.6% (CR = 32.4%; CRh* = 9.2%) within 2 cycles; CR achieved by 60 (32%) subjects (95% CI, 26%-40%); median relapse-free survival 6.7 months for responders

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%): pyrexia (62%), headache (36%), peripheral edema (25%), febrile neutropenia (25%), nausea (25%), hypokalemia (23%), and constipation (20%). Serious adverse reactions in 65% of patients; fatal adverse events in 15%. Serious infections in approximately 25% of patients. Key serious toxicities include cytokine release syndrome and neurological toxicities.
target_moa: Bispecific T-cell engager antibody construct that binds CD19 (expressed on B cells) and CD3 (expressed on T cells), redirecting cytotoxic T cells to kill CD19-expressing precursor B-cell ALL cells
modality: bispecific (bispecific T-cell engager / BiTE antibody construct)

boxed_warning.content: Cytokine Release Syndrome (CRS), which may be life-threatening or fatal; and neurological toxicities, which may be severe, life-threatening, or fatal. Interrupt or discontinue BLINCYTO as recommended.

rems.type: A REMS consisting of a communication plan and a timetable for submission of assessments was determined necessary to ensure benefits outweigh the risks of cytokine release syndrome, neurologic toxicity, and preparation/administration errors.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Durable complete remission (CR) rate, supported by minimal residual disease (MRD) reduction to less than 10^-4 as reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit

citations.quote: This reviewer recommends approval of blinatumomab under 21 CFR 601 Subpart E for the treatment of patients with Philadelphia chromosome negative relapsed or refractory precursor B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia. Approval is supported by the results of Protocol 211 in which 32% (95% CI, 26% - 40%) of patients in the intended population achieved complete remission (CR) with 2 cycles of treatment

Recommended regulatory action
Accelerated Approval based on demonstration of an acceptable response rate with some information on duration

*Subjects on Protocol 211 who achieved CR or CRh* were also tested for MRD using a sensitive molecular method. MRD levels less than 10^{-4} are expected to be reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit in the intended population. In Protocol 211, a reduction in MRD to less than 10^{-4} was achieved by 31% (95% CI, 25%-39%). Using the published proportion of subjects with an MRD response after chemotherapy (30%), and the weighted "CR" rate in the historical controls (24%), the expected rate of an MRD response in remission is 7% (95% CI, 4%-12%). If the actual CR+CRh* rate in Protocol 211 is used (42%), only 23 (12%; 95% CI, 8%-18%) of the subjects in Protocol 211 would be expected to have an MRD response in remission, less than actually obtained using blinatumomab (31%).*

summary.text: BLINCYTO received accelerated approval under 21 CFR 601 Subpart E based on the CR rate from the single-arm Phase 2 trial MT103-211 (CR/CRh* 41.6%; CR 32% [95% CI 26%-40%]). It was granted Breakthrough Therapy designation on 30 June 2014 and had orphan drug designation for acute lymphocytic leukemia granted 5/16/2008. A confirmatory Phase 3 randomized trial (Protocol 00103311) versus standard of care with overall survival endpoint was required to verify clinical benefit.

citations.quote: This reviewer recommends approval of blinatumomab under 21 CFR 601 Subpart E for the treatment of patients with Philadelphia chromosome negative relapsed or refractory precursor B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia. Approval is supported by the results of Protocol 211 in which 32% (95% CI, 26% - 40%) of patients in the intended population achieved complete remission (CR) with 2 cycles of treatment

In the single-arm pivotal Phase 2 trial (MT103-211) in 185 adult subjects with Philadelphia chromosome-negative B-precursor relapsed or refractory ALL, the primary efficacy endpoint complete remission/ complete remission with partial hematological recovery (CR/ CRh*) rate is 41.6% (CR = 32.4%; CRh* = 9.2%) within 2 cycles of blinatumomab treatment.
Blinatumomab was granted as a Breakthrough Therapy on 30 June 2014 for the proposed indication based on data from the main study MT103-211.
Orphan designation for “treatment of acute lymphocytic leukemia” was granted 5/16/2008.
